context:
Use git-filter-repo with a name-callback to target only commits where
author name == b"user.email", leaving all other authors untouched.
Work in strict order: backup → rewrite → verify → re-add remotes → push.
Never push until w4 (verification) passes completely.
Handle the remote-only seed-corpus-infra branch last, via cherry-pick.
description:
On 2026-01-28, a local git config entry `user.name=user.email` was written
to .git/config, setting the commit author name to the literal string "user.email"
instead of "Joe Harris". This was discovered and fixed on 2026-04-14 (the config
entry has been removed). However, all commits between 80e17e9 (2026-01-28 09:21)
and 2cfdcfd (2026-04-14 20:16) were made with the bad author name - a total of
2,286 commits on main and 1,850 commits on published-results (overlapping with main).

git-filter-repo is available at /Users/joe/.local/bin/git-filter-repo and will
be used to rewrite the author name across all affected commits.

Refs affected:
- main: 2,286 commits with author "user.email" (first: 80e17e9, last: 2cfdcfd)
- published-results: 1,850 commits affected (shares history with main)
- Tags v0.1.0-v0.2.0: point to correct-author commits, but their SHAs shift
  during rewrite - tags must be force-pushed after rewrite
- private/claude/seed-corpus-infra: 3 remote-only commits on top of old main;
  these are NOT rewritten by filter-repo and must be cherry-picked onto new main
- claude/condescending-mcnulty: local branch, 0 commits ahead of main - safe to
  reset to new main HEAD after rewrite
- public remote: READ-ONLY by repo policy - must NEVER receive a push

filter-repo behavior to account for:
- Rewrites ALL commits reachable from any local ref (both branches, all tags)
- Strips all remote-tracking refs after rewrite (safety mechanism) - remotes
  must be re-added manually before any push
- Does NOT have a safe --dry-run mode for name callbacks

anti_patterns.dont: proceed past w4 if any verification check fails
anti_patterns.why: push only after confirming the rewrite is correct

anti_patterns.dont: push the backup/* tags to any remote
anti_patterns.why: they're local safety refs only and contain the old 'user.email' commits

anti_patterns.dont: run `git push` or `git push public` without specifying `private` as the remote
anti_patterns.why: this would push to the public repo, leaking private history
filter-repo is irreversible without a backup ref; restoring from backup/pre-author-fix/* is the only recovery path
the second run would find nothing to fix and produce a clean-run, but may corrupt the backup tags
the lease check will always fail since the remote has old SHAs; plain `--force` is correct and intentional

preserves.behavior: Total commit count must be unchanged after rewrite
private/claude/seed-corpus-infra: 3 unique commits must be recoverable and pushed with correct authorship
public remote: must never receive a push at any point during this process
published-results branch: must be rewritten and force-pushed to private with correct authorship
version tags v0.1.0-v0.2.0: must survive the rewrite and be accessible on private remote

scope_rules.path_glob: git refs (branch and tag pointers after rewrite)

verifications.description: No 'user.email' author commits remain anywhere in the repo

work_units.summary: Pre-flight: snapshot current state of all refs
Delete local backup tags after validation
Create backup tags before running filter-repo
Run git-filter-repo to rewrite author name
Verify rewrite correctness before touching any remote
Force-push main and published-results to private remote
Force-push version tags to private remote
Reset local claude/condescending-mcnulty to new main
